sources.title: Introducing Claude 4
sources.evidence: May 22, 2025 launch names Claude Opus 4 and Anthropic; confirms extended thinking, parallel tool use, coding and sustained agent workflows. Reopened on October 27 for the parameter re-audit: the launch and comparison table provide no total or active count or named sized base.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4 & Claude Sonnet 4
sources.evidence: Sections 1 and 1.1 describe hybrid reasoning, visual analysis and tool use. Fresh official copy retrieved October 27 at 10:11:47 UTC and independently inspected from the shared text cache. Sections 1 and 1.1 describe pretraining, post-training and hybrid reasoning without a nominal total or active count or a named sized base. Section 1.1.2 identifies a separate smaller thought-summary model; its undisclosed size is not a reason to reject a nominal Opus 4 count, but none is supplied. Whole-card parameter/size search produced tool arguments, hyperparameters and unrelated text, not model counts.

sources.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Methods explicitly lists production Opus 4 separately from Opus 4.1 and helpful-only variants; interventions operate on layer residual streams. Discussion describes attention heads and transformer-based models. Supports broad transformer classification, without disclosing dense/MoE topology or parameter counts. Reopened October 27: Methods Notes explicitly says helpful-only variants share their respective production model base, but gives no nominal size for the Opus 4 base; layer activations and intervention counts do not establish model parameters.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: API access is governed by restrictive commercial terms; reverse engineering and duplication are restricted and no general intellectual-property rights are granted. Supports the descriptive proprietary classification, not a weight license.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: Anthropic explicitly states that Claude weights are not publicly released or provided to users. Used only for Claude distribution policy, not technical specifications of Opus 4.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4 on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Exact Opus 4 provider documentation lists text/image inputs, text output, a 200,000-token context, function calling and extended thinking. Accessed through the legacy URL after the newer URL returned a fetch error; these are documented specifications, not evidence of current endpoint operation.

sources.title: Citations API and PDF support for Claude models now in Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: June 30, 2025 announcement explicitly lists Claude Opus 4 as supporting PDF document processing through Invoke Model and Converse APIs.

sources.title: System Card Addendum: Claude Opus 4.1
sources.evidence: Fresh official copy retrieved October 27 at 10:18:47 UTC and inspected from the shared text cache. Introduction explicitly identifies Opus 4.1 as an updated version of Opus 4. Neither model has a published nominal size here; the comparison tables report evaluation results, with no activated-parameter column. This named relationship therefore supplies no size to transfer to Opus 4.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.5
sources.evidence: Fresh official copy retrieved October 27 at 10:18:49 UTC and inspected from the shared text cache. Sections 1.1 and 2 and Opus 4 comparisons disclose no total or active count for Opus 4 or named sized-base lineage. Parameter matches concern effort, sampling, hyperparameters or the new_context_tool schema, rather than learned weights.

sources.title: Model deprecations
sources.evidence: Maps Claude Opus 4 to claude-opus-4-20250514 and states retirement on the Claude API on June 15, 2026.

sources.title: Claude Model Pricing — List Prices by Platform, effective May 12, 2026
sources.evidence: Parent checked the exact Claude Opus 4 API pricing table: it lists both 200K and 1M tiers, conflicting with retained model/provider context specifications. The pricing row alone does not establish when or on which access tier 1M was available.

sources.title: Summer 2025 Pilot Sabotage Risk Report
sources.evidence: Fresh first-party search lead opened October 27. Appendix Opus 4’s Continuity with Past Models (PDF pages 42–43) identifies Sonnet 3.7 as the immediate predecessor but says the models differ in several ways and redacts the effective-compute scale-up. This is a qualitative continuity comparison, not identification of Opus 4 as a variant of a nominally sized base. The newer-model appendix describes Opus 4.1 continuity without sizes; no parameter or billion-count disclosure was found.

sources.title: Teaching Claude Why
sources.evidence: Fresh first-party fine-tuning search lead opened October 27. Methods says experiments mainly fine-tune Sonnet 4 or Haiku 4.5 and their bases; the discussion explains safety-training updates from Opus 4 to Opus 4.5. It does not identify a sized base for Opus 4. Dataset-token counts and shared training methods are not parameter sizes.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 4.6
sources.evidence: Fresh official copy retrieved October 27 at 10:18:49 UTC, independently inspected from the shared text cache. Model-training description, comparison material and whole-card size/parameter search yield no nominal total or activated-parameter count for Opus 4. Effort controls, feature activations and research hyperparameters do not supply counts.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Opus 5.5
sources.evidence: Fresh official copy retrieved October 27 at 10:11:48 UTC, independently inspected from the shared text cache. Model description and Table 8.1.A report training characteristics and capability scores, not total/activated parameter columns or Opus 4 sizes. Whole-card search yields no parameter-count disclosure or nominally sized Opus 4 base. Intervening cached Opus 4.7, 4.8 and 5 cards were also searched for parameter and size disclosures without a relevant hit.

name.note: Official launch name; deprecation documentation identifies the exact dated API snapshot.

developer.note: Named developer in the original system card.

family.note: Normalized catalog family for the officially named Claude Opus line.

release_date.note: Explicit public launch date; the 20250514 snapshot suffix is not its release date.

open_weights.note: Exact model launched through hosted products; explicit later Claude-wide weight non-distribution policy corroborates closed weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification of closed commercial access; not an SPDX or downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened original launch/card and interpretability evidence, independently inspected later official cards through Opus 5.5, and searched exact model names with parameter, billion/trillion, base-model and fine-tuning terms. No developer-published nominal total or size-bearing base-model relationship was established. Opus 4.1 is explicitly an updated Opus 4, but neither has a size here; the sabotage report’s Sonnet 3.7 continuity comparison is not sized lineage. Third-party estimates and research activation/dataset counts are not developer specifications. This null reflects absent nominal evidence, not a requirement for a tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately on October 27: original and later first-party cards and comparison tables contain no Opus 4 activated-parameter column or per-token parameter count. Effort/sampling controls and interpretability activation quantities are different measurements. Neither an assumed dense topology nor a total-to-active equality is supported; active count remains undisclosed.

architecture.note: Broad classification supported by exact production Opus 4 inclusion, residual-stream layer interventions and transformer/attention discussion. Dense versus MoE, layer dimensions and production parameter counts remain undisclosed; no feature count is used.

context_window.note: Documented context length for exact Opus 4; no inference of current endpoint availability. A May 2026 first-party API pricing table also lists 1M. Retain the directly documented 200K specification and record the unresolved surface/tier discrepancy; pricing alone does not establish availability.

modalities.note: Text and images confirmed for the model; PDF is a supported document input format. Text-to-speech product features do not establish native audio output.

tool_call.note: Parallel tool use and function calling are explicitly documented.

description.value: Claude hybrid reasoning model for coding, complex reasoning, and long-running agent tasks
description.note: Retains supported coding, reasoning and sustained agent use cases; removes undated flagship wording that implies current positioning.

patch.description: Claude hybrid reasoning model for coding, complex reasoning, and long-running agent tasks
patch.notes: Transformer structure is supported by interpretability research on production Opus 4; dense/MoE topology is undisclosed. No developer-published total or active count, or size-bearing base-model lineage, was established. PDF is a supported document format. The dated snapshot was retired from the Claude API on June 15, 2026; documented specifications do not establish current endpoint operation. An Anthropic pricing PDF effective May 12, 2026 also lists a 1M API tier, conflicting with the retained 200K model specification; availability of that tier was not verified.

sources.label: Anthropic pricing table with conflicting context tier

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter-only re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts after original evidence, later cards and focused named-base research checks. No nominal size or usable sized lineage was established; the continuity study redacts compute details. All other field assessments and existing historical-release/retirement qualifications are preserved.
